title: Go-to-Prod Throttleboard — KPI Thermostat and Surge Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic reference to control traffic and KPI thresholds during the first 72 hours of a major rollout. Treat as the single-pane rapid decision board for on-call, product, and ops leads.

TL;DR:
- Set a KPI thermostat (target / warning / critical) for 5 key signals.
- Run the 3 traffic-sim scenarios before ramping >10% traffic.
- If any critical threshold trips, follow the immediate fallback mapping (traffic -> model -> capacity).
- Post-24h: move from thermostat to trend-based SLO windows (1h, 6h, 24h).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API feature rollouts, staged user cohorts, and beta opens.
- Not intended for full platform-wide infrastructure failures (SRE runbooks cover that).
- Assumes dedicated monitoring dashboards and log-level tracing are present (links in linked_artifacts).

Owners & roles (first 72h):
- Product Lead: Maya Patel (overall go/no-go authority for product behavior)
- Ops Lead: Jordan Lee (traffic throttling, routing changes)
- SRE On-call: Aisha Thompson (infra escalations, capacity tweaks)
- Observability/Analytics: Ethan Cole (KPI calculations, dashboards)
- Incident Commander: Sanjay Rao (tie-breaks and external comms)

KPI Thermostat (primary signals) — quick view (target / warning / critical):
1) 95th percentile latency (inference):  < 220ms / 220-350ms / > 350ms
2) Error rate (5-min rolling) :  < 0.3% / 0.3-1.0% / > 1.0%
3) Token cost per 1k requests (moving avg 1h):  within budget / +10-30% / +30%
4) Prefix cache hit rate:  > 70% / 50-70% / < 50%
5) Queue depth (per-pool):  < 50 / 50-200 / > 200

Notes on interpretation:
- Warning: notify stakeholders, reduce noncritical background jobs, enable tighter batching controls.
- Critical: trigger staged fallback immediately (see mapping).
- All thresholds evaluated on 5-min sliding windows for first 6 hours, then 15-min windows until 72h.

Traffic-sim scenarios (run in staging that mirrors production routing):
A) Cold Spike (synthetic burst to 2x expected peak) — validate autoscale, KV cache warmup, request queuing behavior.
B) Degraded Model Variant (simulate fallback to quantized model) — check output quality regression + latency/cost delta.
C) Regional Failure / Drain (drain 1 region to replicate failover routing) — verify routing fallback and end-to-end latency.

For each sim, capture: latency p50/p95/p99, error taxonomy (model vs infra), cache-hit delta, billing delta. Log results to Jira PRODOPS-4321.

Go / No-Go Quick Matrix (pre-traffic ramp checkpoint):
- Safety check 1: SLOs met in staging sim A for p95 latency and queue depth — PASS/FAIL
- Safety check 2: No critical errors in sim B, qualitative sample pass — PASS/FAIL
- Safety check 3: Observability alerts firing correctly and runbooks resolvable within target MTTR — PASS/FAIL
- Only if all PASS -> proceed to 10% ramp, otherwise pause and triage.

Immediate fallback mapping (critical trip actions):
- If latency critical or queue depth critical: reduce traffic to previous stable cohort (ops -> traffic control), enable aggressive batching window (+50ms) and enable prefix cache bypass for large requests.
- If error rate critical: route traffic to model-stable pool (fallback variant), then progressively downshift to lower-cost/low-latency quantized variant.
- If cost blowout critical: cap high-cost routes (large-context requests) and enable per-token suppression heuristics; notify Finance.

Escalation ladder (contact order):
1) On-call SRE (Aisha) — infra checks (GPUs, throttles, kernel OOMs)
2) Ops Lead (Jordan) — routing/traffic rules, pool adjustments
3) Product Lead (Maya) — feature gating, user messaging
4) Incident Commander (Sanjay) — exec/status comms, postmortem lead

Quick runbook (actions by time):
T-minus: pre-ramp (15m before traffic increase)
- Verify dashboards green (Ethan)
- Re-run quick sim A with 10-minute short burst (Ops)
- Confirm canary group routing healthy (Product)
- Slack channel: #prodops-rollout (notify with checklist)

T+5m (first observations):
- Watch p95 and error rate; if warning -> throttle to hold and investigate
- If warnings persist >10m, apply partial rollback to prior commit

T+30m (stabilize or escalate):
- If stable, move to next ramp step (double cohort)
- If unstable, follow fallback mapping and escalate

T+24h (evaluation window):
- Move from 5-min windows to 1h windows for KPI smoothing
- Run dataset-quality spot-checks (samples vs human baseline)
- Prepare draft post-launch ops note (owner: Ethan)

Communication templates (short):
- User-facing incident blurb: "We're seeing degraded performance for some requests; we've routed traffic through a fallback pathway to restore responsiveness. We'll follow up when fully stabilized."
- Internal status: short bullets: what tripped, action taken, next step, ETA

Post-launch measurements (must-have in first 72h):
- SLA adherence per-cohort (hourly)
- Model output quality regression metrics (sampled human eval) — target < 3% regression
- Cost per 1k requests vs baseline — report to finance daily
- Customer-facing errors and top error signatures (grouped)

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Need a small lightweight synthetic generator that emulates long-context user sessions (ticket: PRODOPS-5908).
- Confirm whether dedicated pool supports graceful preemption by analytics jobs — Jordan follow-up.
- Add a simple 'throttle-as-a-service' UI in Console for product leads (MVP scope).

Appendix: quick copies of CLI snippets (ops) — put in separate crib doc, linked in linked_artifacts.

Endnotes:
- Keep this doc short and actionable. If an action requires >15min of work, create a Jira and move to backlog.
- After stable 72h, convert thermostat thresholds to baseline SLOs owned by SRE and Product metrics.
